title: Food, Nutrition, Balanced Diet and Recommended Dietary Allowances
shortDescription: Functions, classification and sources of nutrients, plus how RDAs and balanced diets are defined.
genZNote: Food is what you eat, nutrition is what your body does with it. RDA is a group goal, not your personal minimum — that's the exam trap.

sections.heading: Food and Nutrition
bullets: Nutrition: the science of nutrients and how the body ingests, digests, absorbs, uses and excretes them. Nutrients: macronutrients (carbohydrate, protein, fat; plus water), micronutrients (vitamins, minerals) and non-nutrients (fibre, phytochemicals).
Functions of food: physiological (energy, body-building, protective/regulatory), social and psychological.

Classification: by function — energy-giving (cereals, fats, sugars), body-building (pulses, milk, eggs, meat, fish), protective (fruits, vegetables, milk); ICMR-NIN uses food groups (cereals and millets, pulses, vegetables, fruits, milk and products, flesh foods, nuts and oilseeds, fats and oils).
Energy values: carbohydrate and protein 4 kcal/g, fat 9 kcal/g, alcohol 7 kcal/g.

sections.heading: RDA and Related Terms
sections.body: India: ICMR–NIN revised Recommended Dietary Allowances and Estimated Average Requirements (2020) for reference man 65 kg and reference woman 55 kg; the "Dietary Guidelines for Indians" (2024) offers 17 guidelines and "MyPlate for the Day". Requirements vary with age, sex, physiological state (pregnancy, lactation), and activity (sedentary, moderate, heavy).

table.caption: Dietary reference terms
rows: Estimated Average Requirement — meets the needs of 50% of a healthy group
EAR + 2 SD — meets needs of ~97–98% of healthy individuals in a group; a planning goal, not an individual minimum
Adequate Intake — when data are insufficient for an RDA

sections.heading: Balanced Diet
bullets: A diet supplying all nutrients in adequate amounts and proportions for health, with a little reserve.

Principles: variety across food groups, energy matching expenditure, protein quality via cereal–pulse combinations, adequate fruit and vegetables, limiting sugar, salt (<5 g/day) and saturated/trans fat.
Typical energy distribution: carbohydrates ~45–60% (WHO up to 75%), protein 10–15%, fat 20–30%.
Meal planning tools: food exchange lists, food pyramids, MyPlate.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: A balanced diet supplies adequate energy and all nutrients in proportion, and RDAs are population-level intake targets set by expert bodies such as ICMR–NIN.

highYieldFacts: RDA is not a minimum requirement for every individual.
commonTraps: Do not equate RDA with EAR.

sources.name: ICMR–NIN Nutrient Requirements and RDA for Indians, 2020

questions.explanation: It covers almost all healthy people in a group.

questions.prompt: ICMR–NIN Dietary Guidelines for Indians (2024) contain how many guidelines?
